description:
The web bundle carries no type hierarchy and no namespace colour table of its own, so what it renders comes from the repository it is showing.

## Background

Two places in the bundle carry vocabulary. The graph view falls back to a hardcoded four-level hierarchy when the configuration endpoint fails, so a repository with a different taxonomy is drawn as though it had this one. The label badge keys its colours off a fixed namespace map and consults nothing — it is not even a fallback, since the app already fetches the namespace list elsewhere and never uses it here.

Both are shipped bundle content naming type names and label namespaces, which the boundary names. Removing them means the view renders what the API served: no hierarchy when the endpoint failed, and colours derived from the namespace list the API already provides.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The graph view carries no hardcoded hierarchy; when the configuration endpoint fails it renders without tiers rather than with invented ones.
- [hard] REQ-02: Label colours are derived from the namespace list the API serves, so a repository's own namespaces are coloured and an unknown one still renders legibly.
- [hard] REQ-03: A repository whose taxonomy matches today's default renders as it does today.
- [hard] REQ-04: No type name or label namespace literal remains in the bundle's rendering paths.

## Notes

The engine's own closed enumerations — issue state and priority — are not adopter vocabulary and are deliberately left alone; their duplication across components is a separate convergence finding.
title: Render the web view without a built-in taxonomy
